specs.label: File ▸ Edit pymolrc — opens the Text Editor window
specs.note: The menubar leaf's edit_pymolrc hook (registered by features/files, resolved by features/texteditor/openEditor) mounts the texteditor overlay slot and opens the `texteditor:@pymolrc` window. In local backend the panel resolves @pymolrc against cmd.tenmol_files, which is not ported, so it surfaces the honest 'not ported' error while still opening a working, editable buffer — the editor window, toolbar, status bar and textarea must all appear.

specs.label: Access badge settles to a concrete filesystem (bridge fs / browser fs)
specs.note: The [data-txted-access] badge starts at 'probing…' then settles once probeServerFiles resolves. In local backend the probe treats the engine's 'not ported' answer as a live route, so it settles to server → 'bridge fs'. The badge must leave the transient 'probing…' state and show a settled label.

specs.label: Path bar shows (unsaved) for an empty buffer
specs.note: The status bar's [data-txted-path] renders the current path, or the literal '(unsaved)' when there is none. In local backend the @pymolrc read fails so the buffer stays pathless; clearing the textarea keeps it that way and the bar must read '(unsaved)'.

specs.label: File ▸ Save button (Ctrl+S) — handler runs
specs.note: Save on a pathless buffer delegates to Save As. In local backend access resolves to server, so it opens a native window.prompt('Save As…') which the headless driver auto-dismisses (returns null) → no write, no crash. The affordance under test is that the button exists and its click handler runs without throwing; actual persistence is covered by the file-service BLOCKED spec.

specs.label: File ▸ Save as … button (Ctrl+Shift+S) — handler runs
specs.note: Save As opens a native window.prompt('Save As…') in server access (auto-dismissed by the headless driver) or a download in browser access. Either way no exception and no console error; the observable write requires the bridge file service (separate BLOCKED spec).

specs.label: Run button is disabled with no server-loaded path
specs.note: Run is enabled only when there is a path AND access==='server'. In local backend the @pymolrc read fails so the buffer is pathless and Run must render disabled — the correct guarded state, not a defect.

specs.label: Syntax ▸ Python radio selects Python highlighting
specs.note: The three syntax radios are exclusive (name=syntax-<key>). Clicking Python must check that radio; the buffer then tokenises with the Python highlighter (keywords/strings/comments).

specs.label: Syntax ▸ PML radio selects PML highlighting
specs.note: Clicking PML must check that radio and switch the underlay to the PML tokeniser (command keyword + argument + # comment + python/embed/skip blocks).

specs.label: Syntax ▸ Plain Text radio selects no highlighting
specs.note: Plain Text is the no-highlighter mode (parity with PyMOL: only python.py/pml.py exist). Clicking it must check that radio; every line renders as a single plain token.

specs.label: Font size input changes the editor font size
specs.note: The Font number input (the Qt 'Select Font…' context-menu entry) sets fontSize state, applied inline to .txted__editor. Setting it to 20 enlarges the code surface. The size change is a CSS style on a non-canvas element, so it is not captured by the objective DOM/canvas diff — flagged needsVisual so a screenshot judge confirms the enlargement; the check here verifies the input accepts the value without error.

specs.label: Font size input clamps out-of-range values (8–24)
specs.note: onChange clamps to Math.min(24, Math.max(8, n||12)). Typing 99 must clamp to 24 (and empty/NaN to 12). The clamped value lives only in the input's value prop (not page text), so this is confirmed visually; the driven check ensures the clamp logic does not throw.

specs.label: Typing in the textarea updates the buffer and marks it modified
specs.note: The textarea is the real editable control; the highlighted <pre> underlay mirrors it. Typing changes both (so body text changes) and, because saved!==text, the '• modified' dirty flag appears.

specs.label: Dirty indicator '• modified' reflects unsaved edits
specs.note: dirty = text!==saved. After a clean start, typing must reveal the [data-txted-dirty] badge reading '• modified'.

specs.label: PML highlighter emits command-keyword and argument tokens
specs.note: With PML syntax selected, a line 'color red' tokenises to a keyword ('color') plus an argument (' red'). The underlay must contain a .tok--keyword span.

specs.label: Python highlighter emits keyword and string tokens
specs.note: With Python syntax selected, 'from pymol import cmd' + a quoted string must produce .tok--keyword (import/from) and .tok--string spans in the underlay.

specs.label: Comment lines render as comment tokens
specs.note: In PML mode a '# ...' line is a comment; the underlay must contain a .tok--comment span.

specs.label: Open with unsaved edits raises the Save-changes guard
specs.note: check_ask_save (TextEditor.py) guards Open when the buffer is dirty: clicking Open must present the Yes/No/Cancel ConfirmPrompt ('Save changes?') instead of proceeding. Leaves the modal open; the following guard specs dismiss it.

specs.label: Save-changes guard · Cancel aborts and closes the modal
specs.note: Cancel closes the guard and aborts the pending Open, leaving the (still dirty) buffer untouched. The ConfirmPrompt must disappear.

specs.label: Save-changes guard · No proceeds without saving
specs.note: No dismisses the guard and continues the pending Open without saving; in local backend the ensuing Open opens a native prompt/picker (auto-handled by the driver). The observable, objective result is that the ConfirmPrompt closes.

specs.label: Save-changes guard · Yes saves then continues
specs.note: Yes runs Save and, on completion, continues the pending Open. In local backend the Save routes to a native Save-As prompt and the Open to a native prompt/picker (both auto-handled by the driver); the objective result is the ConfirmPrompt closing without error.

specs.label: Ctrl+O keyboard shortcut triggers Open
specs.note: onKeyDown maps Ctrl/Cmd+O to the guarded Open. On a clean buffer the guard passes straight through to Open (native prompt/picker in local backend, auto-handled by the driver). The check verifies the shortcut is intercepted (preventDefault) and its handler runs without throwing or logging.

specs.label: Ctrl+S keyboard shortcut triggers Save
specs.note: onKeyDown maps Ctrl/Cmd+S (no shift) to Save. In local backend a pathless Save routes to Save-As → native prompt (auto-dismissed). Verifies the shortcut is intercepted and the handler runs cleanly.

specs.label: Ctrl+Shift+S keyboard shortcut triggers Save As
specs.note: onKeyDown maps Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+S to Save As → native prompt/download in local backend (auto-handled). Verifies the shortcut is intercepted and the handler runs cleanly.

specs.label: Editor window exposes a resize grip
specs.note: The DialogWindow chrome hosting the editor provides a bottom-right pointer-drag resize grip (.dlgwin__grip). Free pointer-drag resize is not expressible in the audit action DSL, so this records the affordance's presence (hoverable grip) rather than the drag itself.

specs.label: Editor window close button dismisses the editor
specs.note: The DialogWindow title-bar close button ([data-close="texteditor:@pymolrc"]) removes the window from the dialogs store; the editor and its textarea must disappear.

specs.label: Open reads a file from the PyMOL host filesystem
specs.note: Opening an actual server file (window.prompt path → cmd.tenmol_files.read_text) requires the bridge file service; unavailable in local backend, so the read cannot be exercised end-to-end here. The click handler and its dirty-guard are covered by the guard specs.

specs.label: Save writes the buffer to the PyMOL host filesystem
specs.note: Writing to the bridge (cmd.tenmol_files.write_text) and reporting 'wrote <path>' requires the file service. In local backend Save falls back to a native prompt/download, so the server write path is untestable here.

specs.label: Run executes the edited script on the PyMOL host
specs.note: Run (cmd.run for .py, cmd.do('@path') otherwise) is enabled only when a path is loaded from the server, which needs the bridge file service. In local backend the buffer stays pathless so Run is disabled (covered objectively by texteditor.toolbar.run.disabled) and cannot be exercised.

specs.label: pymolrc buffer shows the 'restart to apply' note
specs.note: The role=note banner ('pymolrc is read at startup — restart PyMOL to apply…') appears only when the loaded path is a real pymolrc (isPymolrc(path)). That requires resolving/loading the rc file over the bridge; in local backend the load fails so the note never renders.

specs.label: Active-pymolrc chooser lets you switch between multiple rc files
specs.note: When PyMOL loaded more than one rc file, resolvePymolrc returns >1 candidates and the panel offers a [data-txted-pymolrc] <select> to switch (with the same dirty guard). The candidate list comes from cmd.tenmol_files.pymolrc over the bridge; unavailable in local backend.
